newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs steady in down trend.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs steady in down trend.

text.p: Latin American companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) held steady on Monday, bucking the trend of a weak broader market.

Traders said the performance of Latin American ADRs in the wake of a U.S. interest rate hike last week was in contrast to the plunge that took place in 1994, the last time the U.S. central bank raised rates.
"Everything is doing OK, hanging on," said Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities at UBS Securities.
She said investors were "of the view that the Latin American market will still grow even if the U.S. market ... grows more slowly."

Skwarek and other traders said valuations of regional companies still remained attractive relative to U.S. equities and the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond. Mutual funds also were still looking for companies in which to invest.
Brazilian telephone holding Telebras SA rose 1/4 to 103-1/2 in moderate trade that put the ADRs among the most-active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex was off 1/8 to 38-7/8. The company was among the most-active ADRs and volume in all ADRs was light.
The two telephone companies "were part of last week's selloff and I think people with Telmex and Telebras overreacted generally" to the U.S. rate rise, a trader said.
Among other ADRs and foreign shares, Canada's Seagram Co Ltd rose 1/4 to 38-1/2 after its Universal Pictures unit's "Liar, Liar" topped U.S. box office receipts for a second consecutive weekend.
Swedish telephone equipment company LM Ericsson fell 3/16 to 34-1/2.
Decliners swamped advancers 377 to 96 among 806 ADRs. The ADR index dropped 0.68 percent and volume was a light 21 million shares in late morning.
